title: The Educated Barbarian: Meditations analysis (part. 5)
summary: Fifth reading of Marcus Aurelius's Meditations, covering suppressing the thought 'I am hurt', the idea that nothing external can harm the soul, staying objective when insulted, letting reason and the common good guide you, and his frustration that reason now isolates people from society.
claims: Pain is partly constructed by the brain: he feels pain when he hears a joint pop that he would not otherwise feel
Control pain in reverse order: first stop saying you are hurt out loud, since whining only makes you look weak, then stop the thought itself
This applies to injuries from other people like insults and betrayals, not to literally ignoring physical injuries
Do not tie your identity to a job or possessions; then losing them will not crush you and you can rebound quickly
Someone who can disregard others' opinions and venom has a superpower in today's society
When insulted, people lose sight of reality; intellectually dishonest opponents drag you down to fight on their terrain of stupidity
Act according to reason aimed at the good of mankind, and only let others change your mind when it serves justice and the public good, not pleasure or glory
Nihilism and stoicism are the most bastardized ideologies; many self-proclaimed stoics are smug and impervious to critique
It is better to be wrong following a theory you built than right following one someone else put in your head
He worries that in modern society having logic and reason makes people see you as abnormal; he keeps to the path largely out of ego and patience
Keep developing your intellect even if it seems useless or isolating now; the skills may be needed later
